s: A company is running a two-tier web-based application in an on-premises data center. The application layer consists of a single server running a stateful application. The application connects to a PostgreSQL database running on a separate server. The application's user base is expected to grow significantly, so the company is migrating the application and database to AWS. The solution will use Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling, and Elastic Load Balancing. Which solution will provide a consistent user experience that will allow the application and database tiers to scale?
o: Enable Aurora Auto Scaling for Aurora Replicas. Use a Network Load Balancer with the least outstanding requests routing algorithm and sticky sessions enabled.
Enable Aurora Auto Scaling for Aurora writers. Use an Application Load Balancer with the round robin routing algorithm and sticky sessions enabled.
Enable Aurora Auto Scaling for Aurora Replicas. Use an Application Load Balancer with the round robin routing and sticky sessions enabled.
Enable Aurora Scaling for Aurora writers. Use a Network Load Balancer with the least outstanding requests routing algorithm and sticky sessions enabled.
e: Aurora Auto Scaling enables your Aurora DB cluster to handle sudden increases in connectivity or workload. When the connectivity or workload decreases, Aurora AutoScaling removes unnecessary Aurora Replicas so that you don't pay for unused provisioned DB instances

w.y: A "stateful application" that must scale needs sticky sessions so users keep their session, and the read-scaling part of Aurora is Aurora Auto Scaling for Aurora Replicas. Sticky sessions are an Application Load Balancer feature.

o.A: NLBs do not offer the least outstanding requests algorithm.
o.B: Aurora Auto Scaling adds or removes Replicas, not writers.
o.C: Correct: Aurora Replica auto scaling plus an ALB with sticky sessions.
o.D: Aurora cannot auto scale writers, and NLBs do not offer least outstanding requests.
